title: Integral local systems and their normalized reduction towers
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, $A=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring, and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] use the continuous-function coefficient sheaves $A_X$ and $E_X$ of [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients], and write $A_{n,X}$ for the constant sheaf of the finite ring $A/\varpi^nA$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. There are canonical ring-sheaf isomorphisms $A_X\cong\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A_{n,X}$, $A_X/\varpi^nA_X\cong A_{n,X}$ and $A_X[1/\ell]\cong E_X$, compatible with the reduction and inclusion maps. Limits are limits of sheaves, and localization is the sheaf colimit of repeated multiplication by $\ell$.

For a ring sheaf $R$ let $\operatorname{Loc}(R)$ be the full category of sheaf $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] locally isomorphic, for a pro-etale covering, to a finite direct sum of copies of $R$, allowing rank zero and locally varying ranks. Let $\mathcal T_X(A)$ have objects towers $(F_n,t_n)_{n\geq1}$ with $F_n\in\operatorname{Loc}(A_{n,X})$ and $A_{n,X}\otimes_{A_{n+1,X}}F_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_n$ induced by $t_n$, where tensor products are sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Morphisms are compatible families of module maps. Then reduction is an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Loc}(A_X)\longrightarrow\mathcal T_X(A),\qquad M\longmapsto(M/\varpi^nM)_n.$$
A quasi-inverse is $(F_n)_n\longmapsto\varprojlim_nF_n$, with its induced $A_X$-action. The natural maps $M\to\varprojlim_nM/\varpi^nM$ and $(\varprojlim_nF_n)/\varpi^n\to F_n$ are isomorphisms, naturally in modules and towers.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2), Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.4(1), p. 59; the reduction ring identification is the rank-one reduction in this proposition.

proof.text: Construct actual scalar cokernel towers and their functorial maps. The completeness theorem gives normalization and full faithfulness by the universal property of the quotient cone. The effectivity theorem gives essential surjectivity: each projection from a tower limit induces an isomorphism from its scalar cokernel. Choose the resulting equivalence with this fixed reduction functor. Define completion by composing the quotient cone with the counit isomorphism; transport its limit property along the counit. Naturality of the quotient cone proves completion naturality. Quotient naturality applied to the unit and the triangle identity prove the unit projection formula; the counit projection formula is definitional. Fill the four coefficient fields using the constant comparison, coefficient limit, scalar quotient and localization theorems.
